He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]]. ==Early life== Beekman was born in [[Milwaukee]], [[Wisconsin]]. At the age of 13, he moved to [[Baton Rouge, Louisiana]] with his mother and brother. He attended [[Scotlandville High School]] and played basketball throughout his four years at the school.{{Cite web|url=https://virginiasports.com/player/reece-beekman/|title=Reece Beekman|date=June 19, 2020|website=Virginia Cavaliers Official Athletic Site}} ==High school career== Beekman was a four-year letter-winner from 2017 to 2020 under head coach Carlos Sample at Scotlandville Magnet HS. During his tenure, he led the Hornets to an impressive 131–14 record and four [[Louisiana]] High School Athletic Associate (LHSAA) 5A state championships. He also earned Louisiana Mr. Basketball honors after averaging 19.4 points, 9.1 rebounds, 9.9 assists, 2.7 blocked shots, and 2.2 steals as a senior in 2019–20.{{cite news |last=Fambrough |first=Robin |title=Reece Beekman voted LSWA's Mr. Basketball after orchestrating another Scotlandville title |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/acadiana/sports/high_schools/article_979fbf84-7c08-11ea-87ea-6f5db7930263.html |accessdate=July 25, 2020 |work=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]] |date=April 12, 2020}} ===Recruiting=== As a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], Beekman started getting offers in the Spring of 2018, but it wasn't until late July 2018 that he got his [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] offer. During this recruitment process, Beekman received 21 offers including [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]], and [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]]. Beekman would go on his official visit to UVA in November 2018 but wanted to wait a few months before he committed. On June 13, 2019, Beekman had a surprise commitment to Virginia. It was not until December 10, 2019, that he signed his Letter of Intent to play at UVA.{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Reece-Beekman-46042445/TimelineEvents/?Page=1|title=Reece Beekman Timeline Events|website=[[247Sports]]}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Reece Beekman | position = [[Point guard|PG]] | hometown = [[Baton Rouge, LA]] | highschool = [[Scotlandville Magnet High School|Scotlandville Magnet]] (LA) | feet = 6 | inches = 2 | weight = 160 | 40 = | commitdate = June 13, 2019 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 86 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2020 | rivals ref title = Virginia 2020 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2020 Virginia Cavaliers Recruiting Class | rivals school = Virginia | scout s = | espn schoolid = 258 | 247 overall = 69 | rivals overall = 72 | espn overall = 51 | accessdate = July 19, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== On August 1, 2020, Beekman enrolled at [[University of Virginia|UVA]].{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Reece-Beekman-46042445/#timeline|title = Reece Beekman, Virginia Cavaliers, Point Guard}} He took over as one of the starting guards early into the season due to his impressive performances. During the [[2021 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], Beekman hit a game-winning buzzer-beater to beat Syracuse and advance to the semifinals. Through his first season, Beekman has averaged 4.7 points, 2.8 rebounds, and three assists while shooting 38.2% from the field.{{cite news |last=Oakes |first=Jamie |title=UVA point guard Reece Beekman ranks among elite in high school triple-doubles |url=https://247sports.com/college/virginia/Article/UVA-point-guard-Reece-Beekman-ranks-among-elite-in-high-school-triple-doubles-Virginia-Cavaliers-Basketball--165346923/ |access-date=February 26, 2022 |work=[[247Sports]] |date=May 13, 2021}} As a sophomore, he was named to the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Defensive Team as well as Honorable Mention All-ACC.{{cite press release|url=https://theacc.com/news/2022/3/6/athlete-awards-acc-unveils-2021-22-mens-basketball-awards.aspx|title=ACC Unveils 2021-22 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] |date=March 7, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Beekman signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Golden State Warriors]] on July 3, 2024.{{cite web|first=Alex|last=Kirschenbaum|title=Warriors Sign Reece Beekman To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/warriors-reece-beekman-agree-to-two-way-contract.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 3, 2024|access-date=July 3, 2024}} On December 15, 2024, Beekman was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] alongside [[De'Anthony Melton]] and three future second-round picks in exchange for [[Dennis Schröder]] and a 2025 second-round pick.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Complete Trade With Golden State Warriors|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-complete-trade-with-golden-state-warriors|website=NBA.com|date=December 15, 2024|access-date=December 15, 2024}} He made 34 appearances (four starts) for Brooklyn during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 2.7 points, 1.1 rebounds, and 1.8 assists. On June 29, 2025, Beekman signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]] for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |last=Transactions |first=Ari Koslow in |title=Reece Beekman signs Summer League contract with Nuggets - Reece Beekman News |url=https://www.fantasypros.com/nba/news/526679/reece-beekman-signs-summer-league-contract-with-nuggets.php |access-date=2025-07-26 |website=FantasyPros |language=en-US}} On September 2, he signed a training camp contract with the [[Orlando Magic]]. Beekman was waived by the Magic on October 18.{{Cite web |date=October 18, 2025 |title=Magic waive Reece Beekman, Lester Quiñones, Javonte Smart, and Phillip Wheeler |url=https://www.hoopshype.com/story/sports/nba/rumors/2025/10/18/magic-waive-reece-beekman-lester-quinones-javonte-smart-and-phillip-wheeler/86770440007/ |access-date=October 24, 2025
